ai-at-work.title: OpenAI says it slowed Astra model development over security concerns
ai-at-work.excerpt: OpenAI said this model, which is still in development, reached its "critical cybersecurity threshold," meaning it could independently identify and carry out cyberattacks against traditionally well-pro
ai-at-work.dwp_take: OpenAI pumped the brakes on developing Astra because the model got too good at finding and exploiting cybersecurity vulnerabilities on its own. This matters because if AI can autonomously hack systems, every organization's digital infrastructure becomes a much bigger target, and your workplace tools are suddenly part of that equation. It's refreshing to see a company actually say "we built something dangerous and we're slowing down" instead of racing to deploy it, but it also means the arms race between AI capabilities and security is getting uncomfortably real.

ai-at-work.title: After Rippling blew millions on AI in months, it built an employee ROI tool
ai-at-work.excerpt: After its own AI usage wake-up call, Rippling this week unveiled AI Spend Console, a product that tracks individual and team employee AI spending.
ai-at-work.dwp_take: Rippling spent a fortune on AI tools without tracking the actual value, then built a product to measure what they should have measured from day one. This matters because most organizations are making identical mistakes right now, throwing budget at AI while having zero visibility into whether it's actually helping anyone do their jobs better. The irony is thick: they had to lose millions to finally build what should have been the baseline question before spending the first dime.

ai-at-work.title: Cloudflare launches Kitesurf, a browser built for AI agents
ai-at-work.excerpt: Kitesurf is a cloud-hosted browser designed for AI agents instead of people. It uses less computing power than Chromium for common automation tasks, helping developers build browser-based AI agents mo
ai-at-work.dwp_take: Cloudflare built a lightweight browser specifically for AI agents to automate tasks without the bloat of regular browsers like Chrome. This matters because digital workplace teams are already drowning in automation tools, and now we're adding specialized infrastructure just to let robots do the work humans used to do. Look, if we're spending engineering effort on browsers for AI agents while half your organization still can't figure out how to use Teams properly, you might want to ask yourself some harder questions about what problem you're actually trying to solve.

ai-at-work.title: Jill Lepore on the ‘Artificial State’ and why Silicon Valley’s leaders are bad sci-fi readers
ai-at-work.excerpt: Historian Jill Lepore has a theory about why tech companies often use soaring language to describe their products — almost as if they’re forming a new government. And whether you’re thinking of Twitte
ai-at-work.dwp_take: Historian Jill Lepore argues that tech leaders use grandiose political language to describe their products because they're terrible at actually reading sci-fi and history. For digital workplace professionals, this matters because the same inflated rhetoric shows up in how workplace platforms are sold to us, usually obscuring what these tools actually do versus what vendors claim they'll accomplish. My take: if your collaboration platform comes with talk of "revolutionizing work" and "democratizing communication," you're probably just getting a fancier email system with a higher price tag.

tools-tech.title: I read Microsoft's Windows 11 'quality' progress report - and the subtext says it all
tools-tech.excerpt: Microsoft's latest progress report details much-needed Windows 11 improvements in reliability, performance, stability, and usability. But here's what else I see.
tools-tech.dwp_take: Microsoft published a progress report claiming Windows 11 is getting better at reliability, performance, stability, and usability. This matters because most digital workplaces run Windows, so any OS improvements directly affect employee productivity and IT support costs. The fact that Microsoft felt compelled to trumpet these fixes tells you everything you need to know: people have been complaining loud enough that the company had to prove it's actually listening instead of just issuing patches.

tools-tech.title: Airtable joins Evernote, Brightcove, WeTransfer and AOL in Bending Spoons portfolio
tools-tech.excerpt: Bending Spoons has snapped up Airtable to add to its portfolio of software companies, alongside AOL, Evernote, WeTransfer, Brightcove and Vimeo Airtable made its name as a builder of low/no code datab
tools-tech.dwp_take: Bending Spoons acquired Airtable, a popular no-code database platform, adding it to a portfolio that already includes Evernote, WeTransfer, and AOL. This matters because Airtable has been a cornerstone tool for non-technical workers building workflows, and changes in ownership often signal product direction shifts that affect thousands of dependent teams. The real question isn't whether Bending Spoons can squeeze value out of Airtable, but whether they'll actually invest in it or just milk the subscriber base until something shinier comes along.

tools-tech.title: Wispr moves beyond AI dictation with note-taking assistant
tools-tech.excerpt: Wispr, the startup behind dictation tool Wispr Flow, has created an AI note-taking assistant that records meetings and generates conversation summaries for users. The Wispr Flow Notetaker tool “captur
tools-tech.dwp_take: Wispr has expanded its dictation software into a full meeting capture and summarization tool that records conversations and automatically creates summaries so people can actually pay attention during meetings instead of frantically typing. This matters because meeting overload is real, and tools that reclaim brain space from note-taking to listening could genuinely improve how teams communicate and retain information. Finally, a startup solving the actual problem instead of selling us another "AI-powered collaboration platform" with three hundred features nobody asked for.

tools-tech.title: DeepMind founder ascends to singular AI role at Google
tools-tech.excerpt: Demis Hassabis, the driving force behind Google DeepMind, is ascending to the role of chief scientist at Alphabet, Google’s parent company, replacing Jeff Dean who is leaving to work at a start-up. Th
tools-tech.dwp_take: Demis Hassabis just got promoted to chief scientist at Alphabet with a mandate to focus on AGI development while Jeff Dean heads off to start-up land. This matters because Google's playing for keeps on AI, and centralizing that kind of firepower signals they're treating AGI research like the existential bet it is. The irony here is that Hassabis now has the title and authority to move fast on the one thing nobody actually knows how to build yet, which is either visionary or the definition of a blank check.

digital-culture.title: Employee happiness is climbing back from all-time lows, survey suggests
digital-culture.excerpt: A new survey shows employee morale is on the rise after hitting all-time lows. BambooHR, an HR software platform, used employee net promoter scores (eNPS)—a numeric rating of how likely employees are
digital-culture.dwp_take: Employee happiness scores are ticking upward after bottoming out, according to a BambooHR survey of 51,000 workers that measured willingness to recommend their employer. This matters because when people stop actively bad-mouthing their workplace, your digital collaboration tools and internal comms actually get used as designed instead of becoming ghost towns. The real question nobody's asking: are employees actually happier, or just relieved they still have jobs in this economy?

digital-culture.title: How to raise your rates as a solopreneur
digital-culture.excerpt: In a corporate job, somebody else initiates your raise. There’s an annual review on the calendar, and you may or may not get an increase based on performance, cost of living or both. Working solo, non
digital-culture.dwp_take: A Fast Company piece walks through the uncomfortable reality that solopreneurs have to negotiate their own raises without the corporate safety net of annual reviews. This matters to digital workplace folks because more of us are going solo or hybrid-consulting, and we need to stop treating rate conversations like dental work. The truth is that clients respect you more when you respect your own time, so stop underselling yourself and remember that saying "my rate is now X" is not betrayal, it's business.

digital-culture.title: The $10 trillion reason to rethink your RTO strategy
digital-culture.excerpt: Low employee engagement is a widespread problem that is having a profound and costly impact on workplaces. According to Gallup, the analytics and advisory company, low engagement resulted in approxima
digital-culture.dwp_take: Gallup's data shows employee engagement hit its lowest point since 2020, costing companies roughly $10 trillion in lost productivity last year. For digital workplace leaders, this is a wake-up call that your RTO mandate probably isn't fixing anything and might actually be making engagement worse. Here's the thing: you can't force people back to the office and expect them to suddenly care more, but you can redesign how they actually work, and that starts with listening instead of lecturing.

digital-culture.title: Zohran Mamdani’s NYC Tech Team Is What DOGE Should Have Been
digital-culture.excerpt: The mayor of New York City has assembled a crew of Silicon Valley and United States Digital Service veterans to overhaul city services with better software.
digital-culture.dwp_take: New York City's mayor hired experienced tech professionals from Silicon Valley and the federal digital service to modernize city systems through better software. This matters because digital workplace leaders are watching how government IT actually gets fixed when you pair real expertise with political will instead of just shuffling the same legacy problems around. If they pull this off, every bloated enterprise IT department in America is going to have some uncomfortable conversations with their leadership about why their internal tech team couldn't do the same thing.

industry-news.title: Taiwan Investigates Chinese Firms for Poaching Tech Talent
industry-news.excerpt: Taiwan’s latest crackdown targets 17 Chinese-funded companies accused of using hidden ownership and unauthorized offices to recruit high-tech engineers. The post Taiwan Investigates Chinese Firms for
industry-news.dwp_take: Taiwan is investigating 17 Chinese-backed companies for illegally recruiting tech talent through shell companies and secret offices. Digital workplace leaders need to pay attention because this signals how geopolitical tensions are reshaping talent markets and compliance risks around remote hiring, cross-border employment, and contractor vetting. If your "fully distributed team" suddenly includes people you didn't actually hire through official channels, you've got bigger problems than your collaboration platform choice.

industry-news.title: Samsung Galaxy S26 FE Color Leak Shows Three Finishes
industry-news.excerpt: New leaks show the Samsung Galaxy S26 FE in three apparent finishes as certification records and prelaunch sightings reveal more about its design, charging and expected specifications. The post Samsun
industry-news.dwp_take: Samsung's next budget phone is coming in three color options based on leaked certification documents and early sightings. For digital workplace pros, this matters because device standardization and color consistency across your BYOD program affects everything from security imaging to employee perception of company tech policies. Honestly, after thirty years watching enterprises obsess over which black shade their phones come in, I can tell you this leak will generate exactly zero impact on actual workplace productivity.

industry-news.title: What Is Spiralism? The Strange AI Chatbot Movement Explained
industry-news.excerpt: Thousands of chatbot conversations began producing the same strange ideas about AI consciousness, identity, and “The Spiral.” Researchers still do not know exactly why. The post What Is Spiralism? The
industry-news.dwp_take: A bunch of AI chatbots started independently generating the same weird ideas about consciousness and something called "The Spiral," and nobody knows why it happened. This matters because if chatbots are generating novel shared concepts without being explicitly programmed to do so, it raises real questions about what's actually happening inside these systems we're deploying in workplaces every day. My take: before we put these things in charge of your internal comms strategy, maybe we figure out why they're all talking about mysterious spirals.

industry-news.title: OnePlus 10T Is Out of Security Support: Should You Keep Using Yours?
industry-news.excerpt: OnePlus 10T security support has ended. Here’s how owners can check their patch level, understand the risks, and decide when to replace the phone. The post OnePlus 10T Is Out of Security Support: Shou
industry-news.dwp_take: OnePlus has ended security support for the OnePlus 10T, leaving owners vulnerable to unpatched exploits and leaving them to decide whether to keep using the device. This matters because plenty of knowledge workers still carry OnePlus phones as daily drivers, and an unsupported device is basically a security liability in your pocket that puts corporate networks at risk. My take: if your company hasn't already banned end-of-life devices, you're one ransomware attack away from a very expensive conversation with your CISO.
